reason: The paragraph that opens 'For standard queues' states five batches with five concurrent invocations, up to 300 more concurrent invokes per minute, and a maximum of 1,250 simultaneous invokes per event source mapping.
The throttling bullet under Backoff strategy states the gradual backoff by reducing ESM concurrency, retries until the timestamp exceeds the visibility timeout, then the drop.
The note states the function timeout must be less than or equal to the visibility timeout and Lambda validates on create or update and returns an error.
The quote advises a visibility timeout of at least six times the function timeout so Lambda can retry if throttled on a previous batch.
The quote and its context state messages are hidden for the visibility timeout, by default the whole batch becomes visible again after an error, and code must handle repeats.
The two quotes state the single-invocation assumption for standard functions, committing to S3, DynamoDB or SQS before exiting, and not relying on temporary files or internal state.
The quotes mention database connections only and say static initialization is 'often the best place'; 'SDK clients' and the unhedged 'is the place' are not in the quotes.
The quotes state visual workflow orchestration, separate functions per task, and that Step Functions coordinates data flow and handles errors at each step.
On the Kinesis page the quote states BisectBatchOnFunctionError splits a failed batch in two for function errors and splitting does not consume the retry quota.
The quote states streaming functions return payloads up to 200 MB compared to the 6 MB maximum for buffered responses.
Under Bandwidth limits for response streaming the quote states the first 6 MB is uncapped, then a maximum of 2 MBps, and responses never above 6 MB are never capped.

The quote is a pricing example and the page says these examples use US East (N. Virginia) prices (www/lambda/pricing line 268); the claim states $0.008 per GB as a general price without that Region condition.
Under VPC compatibility with response streaming the quote states function URLs do not support response streaming within a VPC.
The quote states support on Node.js managed runtimes and, for other languages, a custom runtime or the Lambda Web Adapter.
The quote names only function URLs and InvokeWithResponseStream; the API Gateway proxy integration path is in the next sentence of the context, not in any quote.
The quote says for synchronous invocations view the error in the response and retry manually, contrasted in context with automatic retries for asynchronous invocations.
The quotes state Lambda runs the function and waits for a response, and InvocationType RequestResponse is synchronous while Event is asynchronous.
The quotas row for synchronous invocation requests per function per Region gives up to 10 requests per second per environment and 10 times the concurrency limit.
The quote states the calling service waits for the response, defines the returned data, and controls the error strategy including retries.
The quote states the status code is 200 when Lambda was able to run the function, even if the function returned an error.
Under Considerations the Immutable configuration bullet states tenant isolation is immutable and can only be enabled when creating a function.
The Environment reuse row gives never reused across tenants with isolation and might be reused across invocations of the same function without.
Under Pricing the quote states a charge per new tenant-isolated environment depending on memory and architecture; the table row says it is additional to standard pricing.
The quote states Lambda routes by a customer-specified tenant identifier so environments serve only the specified end-user or tenant.
The quote states tenant isolation is not supported with function URLs, provisioned concurrency, or SnapStart.
The quotas row Test events (console editor) gives 10, in the Function configuration, deployment, and execution table whose rows are per-function settings.
The quote states requests faster than scaling or at maximum concurrency fail with a throttling error (429 status code).

Default 3 s and 1 s increments are supported, but the claim states 900 s as the maximum without the condition in the next paragraph that Lambda Managed Instances allow up to 5,400 s for async and most ESM invocations.
The quoted quota row itself adds that Lambda Managed Instances allow 5,400 s for async and most ESM invocations; the claim drops this exception and does not scope to standard functions.
The quote states all data in /tmp is encrypted at rest with a key managed by AWS.
The quotas row for /tmp directory storage gives between 512 MB and 10,240 MB in 1-MB increments.
The quote states 512 MB to 10,240 MB of /tmp per environment whose content remains while frozen, providing a transient cache for multiple invocations.
The quote states /tmp storage is temporary and unique to each execution environment.
The services table row for Elastic Load Balancing (Application Load Balancer) gives Event-driven; synchronous invocation.
The services table row for Amazon API Gateway gives Event-driven; synchronous invocation.
The services table row for Amazon CloudWatch Logs gives Event-driven; asynchronous invocation.
The services table row for Amazon Cognito gives Event-driven; synchronous invocation.
The services table row for Amazon DynamoDB gives Event source mapping.
The services table row for EventBridge gives asynchronous for event buses and rules, synchronous or asynchronous for pipes.
The services table row for Amazon Kinesis gives Event source mapping.
